newsitem.title: GERMANY: German soldiers in mock rape video have left army.
newsitem.headline: German soldiers in mock rape video have left army.

text.p: A German army officer said on Saturday eight soldiers filmed in a home-made videotape of German recruits staging mock executions and rapes of civilians while training for a peacekeeping mission were no longer in the army.

Wolfgang Schraut, commander of Jaeger Battalion 571, said the recruits depicted imitating rapes and executions of fellow soldiers posing as civilians while training for a mission in former Yugoslavia could no longer be punished by the army.
"We will not be able to get our hands on them any more," Schraut told Bild am Sonntag newspaper, according to a text of the article released in advance of its Sunday publication.

"They were already released from the army in an entirely normal fashion after completing their military service," said Schraut, who said he was not in charge of the unit when the incident took place in the spring of 1996.
Private network SAT-1 said on Friday it had the tape and planned to broadcast parts this weekend.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe on Friday condemned the "unbelievable behaviour" of the recruits and vowed that swift and severe punishments would be meted out.
Schraut said he did not know of the existence of the videotape until Friday and had learned that it was shown "on occasion in small circles among the comrades".

Schraut said even though the recruits depicted were no longer in the army, army officials were now trying to track down and reprimand the responsible officers who, he said, failed to report the incident when it happened.
A spokesman for SAT-1 in Berlin said the network planned to air the tape on Monday evening but was considering broadcasting the material in its news programmes at the weekend.

Some 3,000 Germans are in the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia. Around 4,000 Germans took part in SFOR's predecessor, the peace Implementation Force (IFOR) but were stationed in nearby Croatia.
Ruehe said in a statement late on Friday there was no excuse for the macabre imitations of rape and execution.

"This unbelievable behaviour is to be completely deplored," Ruehe said. "An investigation was launched immediately. The participants and their superiors can count on most severe consequences and possibly legal action."

The video, which the Defence Ministry pronounced authentic, shows German recruits at the Hammelburg training facility near Wuerzburg pretending to rape and execute a group of recruits who had moments earlier been acting as a group of civilians.
The Defence Ministry said the incident occurred during a break in the training. He said the state prosecutor's office had not yet been contacted.

Ruehe, who has worked hard to help Germany drop its post-World War Two taboo on sending soldiers abroad on peacekeeping missions and rehabilitate the image of the German military in general, said the video was a perverse aberration.

"It is essential and important that our soldiers are realistically prepared before the start of their mission for the situation in a country hit by a civil war," Ruehe said. But the limits of law and decency have to be, and will be, obeyed."

"It will not be tolerated that soldiers posing as civilians during their training allow their fantasies to get out of control during breaks in their training and to pervert the purpose of the training in a drastic and unacceptable way."
